issues.body: `unwritten_integer_lexicals` compares only the set of observed lexical strings with the set written anywhere in the whole sequence. It does not track which written terms are still live or their subject/predicate/graph coordinates. Because `normalize_term` maps distinct terms such as `"0105"^^xsd:integer` and `"+105"^^xsd:integer` to the same term, a defective sparq result that drops one spelling at identical coordinates while retaining the other can normalize to the same single quad as Oxigraph; the retained spelling is in `written`, so the lexical oracle also passes. The added tests exercise preservation directly and canonicalization to an unwritten lexical, but not this loss mode through the full adjudication path.
issues.fix_hint: Track expected live lexical term identities together with quad coordinates and update lifetime, or add an equivalent per-operation preservation oracle that distinguishes legitimate deletion from accidental collapse and recurses through triple terms. Add a mutation/non-vacuity test through the full adjudication path with two same-value spellings at the same coordinates and a simulated sparq snapshot missing one spelling; assert that adjudication rejects it.
issues.title: Full adjudication can still miss loss of a distinct written numeric term

verdict.summary: Round 3 is stagnant: the prior major soundness finding remains unresolved. The full adjudication still normalizes distinct xsd:integer lexical terms before comparison, while the sparq-side oracle only rejects lexicals that were never written anywhere in the generated sequence. It does not require every still-live written RDF term, at its quad coordinates and lifetime, to remain present. The focused tests demonstrate current preservation and detect canonicalization to an unwritten spelling, but none mutation-tests the full check_seed/cross_compare path when one of two same-value written spellings is dropped. Consequently a faulty sparq snapshot may lose a distinct RDF term yet pass both normalization and the lexical oracle.
